canonical_minimum_architecture.scope: minimum architecture for positive robust statewise net value, not minimum architecture for positive expected selection

binary_global_no_go_example.conclusion: No finite deterministic binary task can guarantee positive net adaptive value in every represented world at K=0.30 through this completion-value mechanism. Positive expected value under a skewed world distribution is not excluded.

exact_extremal_ratio_value_reversal.conclusion: The structural ratio increases while guarantee-level ecological value decreases.

validation.latest_arity_extensions: pending latest queued CI at time of receipt creation

includes: explicit finite expected-value ceiling witness tests

claim_ceiling: Robust thresholds are frequency-free, unconstrained expected suprema optimize over arbitrarily skewed priors, and frequency-floor bounds are generally nonsharp. None estimates natural fitness without world frequencies, opportunity survival, and control cost measured in the same system.

robust_expected_boundary.robust: U(C_A)-U(C_F) is the exact worst-state/frequency-free margin.
robust_expected_boundary.expected: sum_x p_x U[T_pi(x)]-U(C_F) can exceed the robust margin when common branches finish earlier.
robust_expected_boundary.implication: Robust viability implies expected viability for every world distribution; failure of robust viability does not imply expected-selection failure.

minimum_robust_cue_arity_example.interpretation: Binary finite routing cannot guarantee repayment at K=0.30, while ternary routing can.

robust_expected_global_capacity.interpretation: K=0.60 is impossible to repay robustly for any finite information architecture, but can be repaid in expectation by a binary task under sufficiently concentrated one-step encounters.

finite_expected_rescue_example.conclusion: Expected repayment is feasible in the finite scope, but requires substantially more one-step encounter mass than the scalable asymptotic threshold.

scalable_expected_rescue_example.conclusion: The asymptotic scalable threshold is lower because the rare branch can carry arbitrarily large fixed burden.

finite_scope_expected_frontier.arity_dependence: none for the supremum when world frequencies may be arbitrarily skewed
finite_scope_expected_frontier.interpretation: Cue arity constrains robust statewise value, while encounter-frequency concentration can substitute for branching capacity in expected value.

inverse_expected_resource_corner_v1.scope: Exact finite deterministic unit-cost target-resolution tasks, binary witness, freely chosen strictly positive world probabilities
inverse_expected_resource_corner_v1.generic_identity: J_exp(K)=min{j>=2:U(1)-U(j)>K}; (n_min,m_min)=(J_exp+1,J_exp), independent of allowed cue arity b>=2
inverse_expected_resource_corner_v1.interpretive_boundary: Expected positive selection is an existence claim over world-frequency distributions, not robust positivity and not an empirical selection estimate
inverse_expected_resource_corner_v1.regression: tests/test_evolutionary_resource_frontier.py has inverse corner, exact binary witness, strict boundary and finite-search tests

encounter_probability_floor_bound_v1.scope: Nontrivial finite deterministic unit-cost target-resolution tasks, universal fixed comparator, each world has probability >=eta, 0<=eta<=1/n
encounter_probability_floor_bound_v1.sharpness: Generally not sharp for strictly decreasing U; valid upper bound only

canonical_example.conclusion: K=0.60 is impossible to repay in expectation under uniform world encounters even though the unconstrained expected supremum exceeds K.

encounter_probability_floor_bound_v1.tests: tests/test_evolutionary_resource_frontier.py: uniform no-go, exact-policy upper-bound controls, invalid probability floors

uniform_world_exact_envelope.interpretation: Uniform encounters over represented worlds materially reduce attainable expected advantage. Decision-equivalent multiplicity can still concentrate early completions; this is not equivalent to a uniform distribution over terminal decisions.
